answer: The grove roots an identity only if its key is certified by a dedicated onyx, a secure element whose private key is generated inside and never leaves the chip, so one module cannot vouch for two identities and renting is useless — you must own the silicon. Every nadir the attacker mints needs its own onyx; bulk purchases drain finite fab supply and bid the unit price up, a cost that grows per head and cannot be split or parallelized. Break: a leaked firmware signing key mints nadirs without silicon.
